enable_auth_method.note: Creates an OAuth/OIDC source (external IdP). Also used for SAML sources via /api/v3/sources/saml/.

create_organization.note: Creates an OAuth2/OIDC provider (not an organization). Mapped to create_organization for compatibility with the canonical ops vocabulary.

saml.description: A SAML Source can allow IdP-initiated logins, and the documentation warns that this request is not verified and may constitute a security risk.
saml.note: Acceptance of unsolicited SAML responses may be expected when this option is enabled; do not flag as a bug unless the test expects strict SP-initiated request binding.

saml.description: Applications with no bindings are accessible to all users by default.
saml.note: Broad access without bindings is documented default behavior, not an authorization bypass.

saml.description: If a client does not request any scopes, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, excluding special scopes.
saml.note: Extra claims in UserInfo/token responses can be by design when scope is omitted.

saml.description: In releases prior to 2025.10, the email scope always set email_verified to true; as of 2025.10 it defaults to false.
saml.note: Differences in email_verified across versions are documented behavior, not necessarily a claim-integrity bug.

saml.description: Different SAML NameID policies intentionally produce different identifier values, including hashed IDs, session-based transient IDs, UPN, distinguishedName, or email.
saml.note: Identity string differences across tests may be caused by configured NameID policy rather than principal-binding failure.

saml.description: Using email address as SAML NameID is discouraged because users can change email addresses by default.
saml.note: Identity changes tied to mutable email-based NameID may reflect configuration choice rather than an implementation bug.

saml.description: Transient SAML NameID is based on the user's session ID.
saml.note: Different NameID values across sessions are expected and should not be flagged as identity collision or instability.

saml.description: When a Source stage resume timeout is exceeded, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning.
saml.note: Do not flag restarted flow behavior after timeout as flow incoherence.

saml.description: Policies bound to stage bindings can be evaluated at flow-planning time or at stage-run time, producing different behavior as context evolves.
saml.note: Different outcomes before and after user identification may be expected depending on binding timing.

saml.description: RP-initiated logout ends only the application session by default; the authentik session remains active unless User Logout stage is added.
saml.source: Single Logout documentation; User Logout stage documentation
saml.note: Remaining logged into authentik after application logout is by design, not a session revocation failure.

saml.constraint: SAML upstream testing in authentik uses a SAML Source, not a SAML Provider. The SAML Source ACS endpoint is /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/, while /application/saml/<application_slug>/sso/... endpoints belong to authentik acting as IdP for downstream SPs. The fuzzer MUST use the source ACS path for saml_login when testing authentik as a broker/SP.

For all SAML login tests, the executor MUST initiate the SP flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo context. authentik documents SP-initiated SSO and the ACS consumes assertions sent in response to an AuthnRequest; sending a fabricated unsolicited ACS POST without first initiating the flow can fail for flow reasons unrelated to the invariant under test.

Allow IDP-Initiated Logins on a SAML Source is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For I1/I3/I5 tests that are meant to validate request-bound behavior, the fuzzer MUST keep allow_idp_initiated disabled unless the test specifically targets insecure IdP-initiated acceptance.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution testing against authentik as SP, the SAML Source must be configured with the expected upstream trust material (for example signing/verification certificate metadata). If trust material is absent or permissive, a successful forged assertion may reflect intentionally incomplete configuration rather than a signature-validation flaw.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, the SAML Source's issuer/entity-id expectation must be configured. If the source is created without a concrete upstream issuer binding, acceptance of a mismatched Issuer can be caused by unset trust configuration rather than a broken issuer check.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a control login through the same SAML Source without expired_assertion=true before the attack login. Without a successful control, a failed expired assertion test cannot be distinguished from broken source configuration or flow setup.

For I2 replay tests on SAML assertions, authentik documentation only explicitly states session tracking for SAMLSession records used for logout and does not document assertion replay cache semantics. The fuzzer SHOULD test both fixed_assertion_id replay and OneTimeUse replay, but MUST interpret results carefully because replay protection behavior is not described in the provided docs.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving Source stage or external SAML source flows, source authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. authentik documents that a User Login stage in the source flow prevents resumption of the original flow and directly authenticates the pending user, which would invalidate atomicity/coherence test assumptions.

For I3 tests involving policy-gated stages in authentik flows, stage-binding evaluation timing matters. Policies are evaluated dynamically by default, but can be precomputed when 'Evaluate when flow is planned' is enabled. The fuzzer MUST avoid interpreting behavior changes caused solely by planned-vs-run-time policy evaluation as session incoherence.

For I3 config-change sequences, authentik may legitimately apply new flow/provider/source configuration to NEW authentications immediately. A valid coherence test must show inconsistent handling of the same logical request/session context, not merely that a later login used updated admin configuration.

For I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format selection materially changes the downstream identifier. authentik documents that persistent NameID becomes a hashed user ID, transient NameID is based on session ID, emailAddress uses email, and other formats may use LDAP-derived attributes with fallback. The fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins or it will create false identity-collision/mismatch results.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross-protocol merge tests, authentik documentation indicates sources and property mappings can use email and other attributes for linking/enrollment flows. The fuzzer MUST verify whether linking/enrollment behavior is enabled in the source flow before treating account merge as a bug; some merges may be by-design source linking behavior.

Email-based NameID is documented as unstable because users may change email addresses. The fuzzer MUST NOT treat identity changes caused by configured email-address NameID as proof of an I4 collision unless email mutability is controlled in the test setup.

For I5 saml_no_conditions and saml_no_audience_restriction tests, authentik docs do not state that Conditions/AudienceRestriction are optional or ignored. The fuzzer SHOULD test missing Conditions and wrong/missing AudienceRestriction explicitly, but MUST use a control assertion first because failures may also stem from unrelated source or flow configuration.

When using /application/o/userinfo/ as verify_granted_identity after SAML login, the session token must be an OAuth access token obtained from authentik, not the SAMLResponse itself. UserInfo is an OIDC endpoint returning claims for a valid access token.

authentik's token revocation endpoint is /application/o/revoke/ and uses form-encoded OAuth parameters. The fuzzer MUST send the explicit token value in the request body and MUST NOT model logout via browser sign-out URLs as revoke_session, because those are front-channel logout flows rather than direct token revocation APIs.

The OAuth introspection endpoint can only introspect a token from the same provider used to authenticate, unless the token is first exchanged for a token from that provider. The fuzzer MUST keep provider context aligned when using introspect_token or it may observe false negatives unrelated to token validity.

When no OAuth scopes are requested, authentik treats the request as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. For I5 least-privilege tests using OAuth verification after SAML login, the fuzzer MUST request explicit minimal scopes; omitting scope broadens claims by design and can look like over-granting.

Refresh tokens are not returned by default starting with authentik 2024.2; offline_access must be configured and requested. The fuzzer MUST NOT assume refresh-token presence in token responses when verifying post-SAML OAuth sessions.

User Login stage session duration has a numeric sentinel: seconds=0 means the authentik session expires when the browser is closed, not 'immediately invalid'. Different browsers may still retain session cookies. Never interpret seconds=0 as a guaranteed zero-lifetime session for I2 freshness tests.

Authenticator Validation stage last validation threshold has a numeric sentinel: a non-zero value enables less-frequent MFA validation, while the default zero means validation is required every time. For code-based devices, values lower than seconds=30 cannot be used reliably. Do not use sub-30-second thresholds in MFA-bypass or freshness tests.

Email Authenticator Setup stage token expiration is in minutes and defaults to 30. The fuzzer SHOULD account for this when testing alternate-flow MFA interactions; a still-valid emailed code is by design reusable within its validity window unless additional one-time semantics are documented elsewhere.

For SAML tests against authentik as SP, use the ACS endpoint `/source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/` and initiate the SP flow first so the forged SAMLResponse carries the correct InResponseTo. Sending a standalone fabricated POST without first starting the flow will be rejected for flow/session mismatch rather than the target invariant.
saml.source: SAML Source docs; SAML assertion/ACS glossary

saml.constraint: Allow IDP-initiated logins is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For I3/I1 tests that require request-bound verification, do NOT enable IDP-initiated logins; use SP-initiated flow through the ACS path instead.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing, authentik documentation states SAML Source supports signed requests, but the supplied docs do not expose a REST API field for signature-validation toggles. The fuzzer MUST treat signature-validation configuration as undocumented/UI-only and avoid assuming any default validation flags can be set by API.
saml.source: SAML Source index; SAML provider docs

saml.constraint: For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch tests, configure the SAML source with a concrete IdP issuer/entity ID in the source settings. If issuer/entity ID trust is left ambiguous from imported metadata or UI defaults, a passing or failing result may reflect setup ambiguity rather than issuer validation behavior.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion tests, include a CONTROL login with a normal assertion first. Without a successful control, rejection of the expired assertion cannot be distinguished from broken source/provider setup.
saml.source: SAML assertion/ACS semantics; attack-pattern guidance cross-referenced with authentik SAML source flow

saml.constraint: For I2 replay tests (OneTimeUse or assertion ID replay), authentik documentation in the supplied corpus does not state whether replay caches or assertion ID tracking are implemented. The fuzzer SHOULD run two identical saml_login events against the same source and interpret acceptance of the second assertion as a potential finding, but must not assume replay protection is configurable via documented API.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving external sources embedded via Source stage, the source's authentication/enrollment flows MUST NOT contain a User Login stage. authentik documents that doing so causes the source flow to authenticate directly instead of resuming the original flow, which would invalidate session-bound flow-coherence testing.

For I3 source-resume tests, the Source stage has a resume timeout. If the user returns after this timeout, the suspended flow restarts from the beginning by design. Do NOT flag this as a coherence bug; only flag inconsistent handling within the same still-valid suspended flow.

For I3 tests involving policy evaluation timing, authentik stage bindings can evaluate policies either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test must control this setting; otherwise differences after identification/authentication may be by design because later-stage context becomes available only at run time.

For I4 identity-binding tests, NameID format materially changes the identifier authentik receives: persistent maps to hashed ID, transient maps to session ID, emailAddress maps to email, Windows maps to UPN, and X509SubjectName maps to distinguishedName with fallback behavior. The fuzzer MUST hold NameID policy constant across compared logins or results are not comparable.

For I4 email-binding collision tests, avoid using email-address NameID unless the test intentionally targets email-based identity binding. authentik explicitly warns that email-based NameID is mutable by default and recommends against using it as a stable identifier.

For I4 cross-protocol or cross-source merge tests, authentik sources can be shown in the Identification stage and may auto-redirect when only one source is configured and no user fields are selected. The fuzzer MUST ensure the intended source path is actually exercised; otherwise a login may be redirected automatically and confound source-specific identity-binding results.

For I5 SAML authorization-binding tests, authentik SAML property mappings are expression-driven and can emit arbitrary attributes. The supplied docs do not define exact-match, glob, or regex constraint parameters for inbound SAML attributes on the SP side. Therefore the fuzzer MUST NOT invent wildcard semantics for SAML attribute constraints; treat inbound attribute-binding controls as undocumented in this corpus.

When using `/application/o/userinfo/` as verify_granted_identity in SAML profiles, remember this endpoint is OIDC-based and requires an OAuth access token. Pure SAML source login does not itself document issuance of an API bearer token in the supplied docs. Do NOT schedule UserInfo verification after saml_login unless the test flow explicitly obtains an OAuth access token through a documented token flow.
saml.source: OAuth2 provider endpoints; UserInfo glossary; SAML source docs

saml.constraint: Numeric sentinel analysis: authentik documents `Session duration` default as `seconds=0`, meaning 'expire when browser closes', not a positive default TTL. It also documents `Stay signed in offset` default `seconds=0` as disabled, and `Remember device` only applies when set above 0. Never treat 0 as 'use platform default nonzero lifetime' for these fields.

Numeric sentinel analysis: Authenticator Validation `Last validation threshold` uses non-zero to enable less-frequent MFA validation; zero means validate every time. Never treat 0 as 'use default grace period'.

SAML source setting 'Allow IDP-Initiated Logins' is explicitly documented as a security risk because the request is not verified. For I3/I1/I2/I5 SAML tests, the fuzzer MUST distinguish SP-initiated ACS testing from IdP-initiated mode. Do NOT treat successful IdP-initiated login as proof that request correlation or request-bound verification is enforced.

For all SAML ACS tests against authentik, the executor MUST initiate the SAML flow first and preserve RelayState/InResponseTo correlation. authentik documentation describes the ACS at /source/saml/{source_slug}/acs/ and SAML POST handling in flow execution; sending a fabricated unsolicited response without starting the flow can be rejected for flow reasons rather than security validation reasons.

For I1 saml_cert_substitution default-config testing on authentik SAML Source, the fuzzer MUST test whether signature validation is actually configured on the source and MUST compare against a control configuration. The docs state authentik as SP supports signed requests and uses configured metadata/certificates, but do not document insecure defaults for response validation; a failed forged-cert login may simply reflect configured trust, while a successful one would be significant.

For I1 saml_issuer_mismatch testing, the fuzzer MUST vary the SAML assertion Issuer independently from transport endpoint and include a control login with the expected IdP metadata/entity configuration. The docs expose 'Issuer/Entity ID' as a configured federation identifier for SAML sources; without a control, rejection may be due to generic source misconfiguration rather than issuer validation.

For I2 saml_assertion_id_replay and saml_one_time_use_replay, include a baseline successful SAML login first, then replay the SAME Assertion/@ID using fixed_assertion_id across two saml_login events. Because authentik flows are session-based and ACS processing is tied to flow execution, replay failures without a baseline cannot distinguish replay protection from broken setup.

For I2 saml_expired_assertion, the sequence MUST include a CONTROL login using a non-expired assertion before the expired_assertion=true attempt. Otherwise LOGIN_FAILED cannot be distinguished from broken SAML source/provider setup.

For I3 flow-coherence tests involving Source stage or external SAML source flows, authentik documentation states the Source stage suspends the current flow and resumes it later using a dynamic in-memory stage, with a configurable resume timeout. The fuzzer MUST keep both steps within the same resumed flow context and MUST NOT interpret timeout-triggered restart as a security failure.

For I3 tests that modify source/provider/flow configuration mid-sequence, authentik documentation states policies may be evaluated either when the flow is planned or when the stage is run. A valid coherence test MUST show inconsistent handling of the same logical request under unchanged planning assumptions, not merely that a newly planned flow used updated configuration.

For I3 tests involving logout/session invalidation, authentik distinguishes authentik-session logout from provider-only invalidation. The default-provider-invalidation-flow does not include User Logout by default, so RP-initiated logout may end only the application session while the authentik session remains active. Do NOT flag surviving authentik session after provider logout as a bug unless the flow was explicitly configured for full Single Logout.

For I2 freshness tests on authentik browser sessions, User Login stage 'Session duration' has sentinel semantics: seconds=0 means expire on browser close, not an immediately invalid session. Never interpret 0 as literal zero-second lifetime.

For I2 MFA freshness tests, Authenticator Validation stage 'Last validation threshold' has sentinel semantics: zero means validate every time; non-zero relaxes re-prompting. Never assume 0 disables MFA checks.

For I2 email authenticator tests, Email Authenticator Setup stage 'Token Expiration' defaults to 30 minutes. Freshness tests using emailed codes must account for this configured validity window rather than assuming single-use or immediate expiry.

For I4 principal-binding tests on SAML, authentik documentation states NameID is an identifier in the assertion and may be persistent, transient, email address, UPN, distinguishedName, or hashed ID depending on policy/mapping. The fuzzer MUST record which NameID policy is configured before interpreting identity merges or splits; different NameID formats are by-design different identifier strategies, not necessarily collisions.

For I4 saml_email_binding_collision and cross_protocol_identity_merge tests, authentik documentation notes users are often matched/linked by email in multiple federation contexts and warns that email-based NameID can change. The fuzzer MUST test both NameID and email variations with controls and MUST NOT assume NameID is the sole binding key.

For I4 tests using transient NameID, authentik documentation states transient NameID is based on the user's session ID. Repeated logins producing different NameIDs under transient policy are BY DESIGN and must not be flagged as identity instability.

For I5 authorization tests on OAuth/OIDC tokens obtained after SAML-brokered login, authentik treats requests with no scopes as if all configured scopes were requested, except special scopes. Therefore the fuzzer MUST explicitly request a minimal scope set when testing over-granting; omitting scope broadens claims by design and can create false positives.

For I5 tests involving refresh tokens, authentik 2024.2+ only returns refresh tokens when offline_access is configured and requested. Do NOT treat absence of refresh_token as a security control or failure unless offline_access was explicitly enabled and requested.

For I5 tests using UserInfo as oracle, remember that UserInfo reflects granted scopes and mappings, not raw upstream SAML attributes. Missing claims may be due to scope mapping configuration rather than secure filtering of the SAML assertion.

environment_defaults.api_pattern: authentik REST API follows /api/v3/{app}/{model}/ pattern. All CRUD operations use this pattern with standard HTTP methods (GET/POST/PUT/PATCH/DELETE).
